title: 1.3 Continuity

icans: I can decide whether a function is continuous at a number using the three conditions.
I can find the intervals where a function is continuous and remove a removable discontinuity.
I can use the Intermediate Value Theorem to show that a function has a zero.

vocab: f(c) is __________, the limit of f(x) as x → c exists, and the limit equals f(c)
a discontinuity at c where the limit exists, so it can be removed by defining or _____________ f(c)
if f is _____________ on [a, b] and N is between f(a) and f(b), then f(c) = N for at least one c in (a, b)

blocks.p: For each graph near x = c, check each condition.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Continuity at c: f(c) is defined, the limit as x → c exists, and the limit equals _______________.

blocks.stem: f(x) = 3x − 1 if x < 1;  4 if x = 1;  4x if x > 1. Is f continuous at 1?

notes: Removable discontinuity: the limit exists, so the discontinuity can be removed by defining or _______________ f(c).

blocks.stem: f(x) = (x² − 9)/(x − 3). Where is f discontinuous, and how can the discontinuity be removed?
f(x) = 2x + 1 if x ≤ 2;  kx² − 3 if x > 2. Find k so that f is continuous at 2.

notes: Continuous functions: polynomials are continuous everywhere; rational functions are continuous on their _______________.

blocks.stem: Where is R(x) = (x² − 4)/(x² − 9) continuous? Which discontinuities are removable?

notes: Intermediate Value Theorem: if f is continuous on [a, b] and N is between f(a) and f(b), then f(c) = _______________ for at least one c in (a, b).

blocks.stem: Show that f(x) = x³ + 3x − 5 has a zero in [1, 2].
f(x) = x² if x < 1;  2 if x = 1;  2x − 1 if x > 1. Is f continuous at 1? If not, what kind of discontinuity is it?

(AP® Practice) For what value of k is f(x) = kx + 1 if x ≤ 3;  x² − 2 if x > 3 continuous at x = 3?
(A) 1   (B) 2   (C) 7/3   (D) 3
